methodological_rigor.justification: Ambispective multicenter study (17 European centers) analyzing CLDN18.2 expression and clinical outcomes in 563 GEA patients. Biomarker assessment via IHC locally performed; NGS centralized in 123 patients (21.8%). Kaplan-Meier estimates for OS/PFS with Cox proportional hazards models. Two-sided α=0.05. Limitations: retrospective design with local biomarker assessment (no central review), missing data (35.9% EBV, 31.3% PD-L1), spatial heterogeneity (primarily primary tumor samples), incomplete treatment documentation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Observational cohort study of CLDN18.2 prognostic/predictive value in advanced GEA from treatment-naive and treated populations. LoE 2b: individual cohort study. Clinical relevance: addresses unmet need determining optimal therapy (chemoimmunotherapy vs. zolbetuximab) in CLDN18.2-positive disease; trend toward poorer IO outcomes (mOS 16.0 vs 43.0 months, HR 2.04, P=0.052) clinically significant if confirmed.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-aligned reporting with comprehensive baseline tables, molecular profiling summary, and outcome Kaplan-Meier curves. Molecular testing protocols detailed (VENTANA CLDN18, MMR/EBV/PD-L1 per guidelines). However, no statement on data sharing; local biomarker determination introduces measurement heterogeneity not addressed; missing EBV (64.1%) and PD-L1 (31.3%) introduce substantial bias.

novelty_literature.justification: Characterizes CLDN18.2 prevalence (48.3%) and biomarker overlap in European GEA cohort, higher than pivotal trials (24-33%). Novel finding: CLDN18.2-high trend toward poorer IO outcomes (HR 2.04, P=0.052), potentially reflecting immunosuppressive microenvironment. Clinical guidance for HER2+ CLDN18.2-high (improved HER2-targeted therapy outcomes, mPFS 17.0 vs 8.9 months, HR 0.42, P=0.03) actionable but requires larger sample.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear presentation with effective figures showing biomarker overlap and treatment-stratified outcomes. Discussion appropriately addresses regional differences vs. Asian cohorts and mechanistic hypotheses regarding immunosuppressive CLDN18.2-positive TME. Some redundancy between main text and supplementary results.

key_strengths: Large European multicenter cohort (n=563) with 48.3% CLDN18.2-high, higher prevalence than pivotal trials
Identifies CLDN18.2-high + HER2+ subset with improved outcomes on HER2 therapy (mPFS 17.0 vs 8.9 months, P=0.03)
Trend toward poorer IO outcomes in CLDN18.2-high (HR 2.04 for OS, P=0.052) clinically significant if confirmed
Comprehensive biomarker overlap analysis: 21.5% coexpressing CLDN18.2 + other markers
key_concerns: Retrospective design with local biomarker determination (no central review) introduces measurement error
Severe missing data: 64.1% EBV, 31.3% PD-L1, >50% Ki-67; missing EBV particularly problematic given enrichment in EBV+ disease
HER2+ CLDN18.2 analysis underpowered (n=46 total, 31 CLDN18.2-high); wide confidence intervals (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.18-0.97)
IO outcomes trend not statistically significant (P=0.052); risk of Type I error given multiple comparisons
Spatial heterogeneity unaddressed: ~92% primary tumors may not reflect metastatic disease biomarker profile
No mechanistic data on immunosuppressive TME in CLDN18.2-high; hypothesis speculative
chief_reviewer.rationale: Real-world outcomes study documenting higher CLDN18.2 prevalence and potential IO resistance in European GEA cohort. Findings suggestive but require larger prospective validation. Suitable for Tier 3 with major revisions addressing missing data bias, central biomarker review, and underpowered subgroup analyses.
